analysis.title: Something Is Very Wrong Beneath The Surface Of Tech
key_insights: Tech implied volatility has risen about 40% in a little over a month while NDX is roughly unchanged. VXN was near 20 in mid-September and is near 28 now.
VXN is sharply outperforming VIX as hyperscaler CDS spreads widen. AI credit risk is being repriced in tech options while headline equity indices stay resilient.
Per GS, the NDX/SPX volatility spread reached the 98th percentile of its five-year range after last week's tech-led selloff. Thursday's widening was the second largest in five years.
The weekly NDX straddle has moved from pricing roughly 1.5% moves to around 3%, a doubling of implied weekly moves in a few weeks.

SPX downside skew has surged, but client flows show less demand for downside protection than expected. GS attributes this to historically low net exposure, which leaves investors with less need to hedge.

The GS Momentum basket has recorded 30 daily moves of more than 5% in either direction in 2026, more than any other year in the dataset including 2000, 2009 and 2020, with two months of the year left.

sector_views.rationale: No rating is given. The note documents a sharp rise in tech implied volatility and relative tech fear while the index level is unchanged.

risk_factors: Widening hyperscaler CDS spreads are feeding into tech volatility.
Index-level calm may hide stress in tech, with relative tech fear approaching historical extremes.
Momentum traders are facing a record year of violent swings.
